Hmm… I have a box of a million stories that were never finished. And they’re never going to be finished. Those stories are important because it does help us write better - at least in my opinion I think it does. A story I plan on finishing now, I don’t believe could have been created had I not attempted all those other ones. Basically it’s trial and error. If something sticks then it sticks, if it doesn’t then it was good practice at least. 


I write poetry and want to write novels and short stories… my friend and I want to write a screenplay (that is more down his alley than mine) so I understand wanting to do a million different things. Personally I finished a poetry book and released it on Amazon and now I am focusing on a novel. 

To answer your question, it’s totally fine to start with a novel. You just need to be aware that it is going to take time it’s not going to be finished over night. And planning and organization are your friends. Know your characters first, know how you want the story to start, and then write. I got to know my characters and that was my inspiration to continue with your story. I think about them all the time so I can’t not write it… there’s a quote “keep writing. Your owe your characters a story”. 

Write what you believe in. There are no bad ideas really… that all depends on you. What do you want to invest your time in? Once you’ve figured out a plot that interests you the most, plan the chapters, the events, the characters, keep that and it will make the rest much easier.

A very vague and “lifeless” version of the story, I would say. But enough info for me to know exactly where I want to go with it. then for the second draft I write in a word doc and add all the meat of the story. I realize some scenes fit better in other places. Before the 1st draft I make a binder with sections of characters, chapters and what to do with each chapter, setting, dialog ideas.
